doc.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: When Milt knew he had made it
summary: Mona says Milt is still striving and never feels he has arrived.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Can I ask you about some of the early days, you know, Milt is probably the most revered bass player living today. Can you tell us that time when you felt like he had really

established himself. What were some mile markers? Because I spent some time with Dizzy and he told me of a little time, I ask him when did you think you’d made it. And he told me this is when I thought I was there. Can you tell us a time like that about Milt?
I don’t think so because he’s still striving. I don’t know whether he feels he has reached that point yet or not. I really don’t.
He doesn’t. I think you’re right.

I don’t think he does. Because as he says, every time he plays I means he gives it the best shot that he can. And I think he still does that. So I don’t really know if he ever feels that he’s really made it.

Well I didn’t mean that to say in a way that he would relax and say oh I’m there, I don’t really have to work anymore, but when he began to get some feedback from other musicians, that hey, you’re doing it.
